title: Beyond the 956: Peter Hernandez, Bruno Mars' father and 'Dr. Doo-Wop' musician, dies at 74
excerpt: Peter Hernandez, the musician known as "Dr. Doo-Wop" and the father of Bruno Mars, has died at 74. Mars announced his father's death on November 19, 2026, saying his dad "taught me everything I know, especially when it comes to music."
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Peter Hernandez, the musician known as "Dr. Doo-Wop" and the father of Grammy-winning superstar Bruno Mars, has died at 74.

Mars announced his father's death on Thursday, November 19, 2026, in an emotional post on Instagram, sharing a photo of himself hugging his father in a hospital bed alongside throwback pictures of the two of them through the years.

"Last week I got to hug my father one last time," Mars wrote. "If you've ever seen me talk about him I've always said that he's the man that taught me everything I know, especially when it comes to music."

"He raised my four beautiful sisters, my brother, and me. In my eyes he was the greatest dad in the world, and I will miss him everyday until we meet again," Mars wrote. "I Love you Pops. Kiss mom up there for me," he added, referring to his late mother, Bernadette, who died in 2013.

Originally from Brooklyn, New York, Hernandez grew up surrounded by music. He rebranded himself as "Dr. Doo-Wop" at 13 and later formed a band, the Love Notes, which grew to as many as 18 people in Hawaii. The band was inducted into the Doo-Wop Hall of Fame in 2014.

In the 1990s, Hernandez helmed a show at the Sheraton Waikiki Hotel in Hawaii, performing with the band and bringing all of his children on stage with him. Those performances helped young Bruno develop his mini-Elvis persona, which led to a cameo as "Little Elvis" in the 1992 film Honeymoon in Vegas when he was 6 years old — and helped launch his musical career.

Mars, whose legal name is Peter Gene Hernandez — the same as his father — has often credited his dad with shaping his sense of style and sound, from the pinky rings and pompadour to the rhythm he learned playing bongos as a child.

No cause of death has been released. Hernandez is survived by his children: Bruno, his brother Eric, and sisters Tiara, Tahiti, Presley and Jaime.

Sources: People; USA Today; Page Six.
